summary: Data Mover: Databricks connections and sensitive-data guardrails
description:
A pipeline owner can save a Databricks workspace connection, select compute, check its readiness,
start an eligible stopped cluster, and move reviewed data to or from Unity Catalog Delta tables.
Sensitive metadata, unresolved column actions, incomplete scans, and unsupported routes block the
transfer before destination staging. Completed runs explain what was scanned, transformed, and
committed without displaying sensitive values.

First-release scope:
- Authentication: Workspace personal access token; encrypted owner-scoped bundle; replacement and revocation. Deferred: interactive user OAuth and OAuth M2M.
- Compute: Existing SQL warehouse or Unity Catalog-compatible all-purpose classic cluster. Deferred: Jobs compute, notebook/job submission, compute creation, resizing, automatic shutdown.
- Objects: Unity Catalog base Delta tables; fully qualified catalog/schema/table identity. Deferred: Legacy Hive metastore, views, materialized/streaming tables, foreign tables, arbitrary SQL.
- Sources: One consistent query result, bounded batches, full worker scan and encrypted spool. Deferred: Unbounded extracts, incremental/CDC transfers.
- Destinations: Managed Delta table creation, append, full replace; modes enabled only after publication evidence. Deferred: Upsert/MERGE, direct batch-by-batch writes to the live target, external storage credentials.
- Guardrails: Unity Catalog markers, existing SSN scan, Hash/Remove, value-free run review. Deferred: New content detectors, tag editing, physical erasure/retention management.

Planning reference: DBX-EPIC; tracker key not assigned.
Epic guide: [Databricks connections and sensitive-data guardrails](../../docs/stories/databricks-connection-epic.md)
Task backlog: [Databricks implementation tasks](../../docs/stories/databricks-connection-tasks.md)
acceptance_criteria:
- Databricks personal access tokens are encrypted, owner-scoped, replaceable/deletable and absent from definitions, URLs, diagnostics and logs.
- Management-only validation reports compute state without submitting SQL or initiating startup; SQL readiness is a distinct result.
- Explicit and opted-in startup obey owner/provider permissions, compute binding and persisted readiness deadlines; driver-triggered startup races cannot bypass authorization.
- Only supported Unity Catalog base Delta tables, compute combinations, scalar types and create/append/full-replace modes are available; unsupported objects and modes are rejected.
- Catalog, schema, table and column metadata coverage is verified or fails closed; exact configured markers and every class.* column classification produce safe findings without reading classification samples.
- Sensitive source parent/table markers block before extraction; sensitive destination parent/table markers or unavailable target metadata block before staging.
- The worker scans one consistent complete source result in bounded encrypted batches and publishes those exact reviewed batches without re-reading the source.
- All flagged columns require Hash/Remove actions bound to source/target identity and mapping; missing columns, all-column removal, policy drift and unsupported removal cases block writes.
- Hash transforms incoming values with the existing scoped HMAC; Remove omits current output values/schema while preserving target governance and disclosing Delta history/physical-retention limits.
- Delta publication uses private transformed staging and proven atomic operations; conflicts, uncertain commits and cleanup failures have truthful outcomes without blind uncertain-append replay.
- Run review and compute audits retain safe identities, counts, actions, scan coverage and outcomes without source values, raw tags, secrets, tokens or fetch links.
- Provider and compute controls default to enabled; live transfers require explicit metadata visibility verification and writer prerequisites. Flag values do not replace automated, isolated live, operational, annotated-screenshot, or release acceptance evidence.
